stories.title: Hamas agrees to deal for disarmament, Israel's withdrawal
stories.summary: Hamas has said it agreed to a deal to end the war with Israel that included provisions addressing its weapons and the gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces from Gaza. The group's disarmament has been one of the key sticking points in the advancement of a ceasefire deal that has been in place in Gaza since October. US President Donald Trump announced late last night an agreement for the "complete disarmament" of Hamas, calling it a critical step toward a new Palestinian government in Gaza. Hamas officials said that a committee established by Mr Trump's 'Board of Peace' to govern Gaza would oversee the process of storing the Islamist movement's weapons.

stories.title: Meath woman wins Best Dressed title at Galway Races
stories.summary: Lisa Walsh from Dunboyne, Co Meath was named the winner of the Best Dressed award on Ladies' Day at the Galway Races. There were 20 women shortlisted by judges as they wandered Ballybrit throughout the day, tapping those on the shoulder who were standout contenders for the Best Dressed title. That list was whittled down further and 10 finalists took to the stage later in the afternoon. Ms Walsh was eventually chosen as the winner with a dress by Australian clothing brand 'only one ashley' while her hat and bag were hired.

stories.title: EU Commissioner accepts fisheries facing challenges
stories.summary: Minister for the Marine Martin Heydon and the EU Fisheries Commissioner Costas Kadis have responded to warnings from two of the country's leading fishing organisations that the sector is in crisis and will not survive without urgent support from the Government and EU. They were speaking as fisheries ministers from 27 EU states gather in Cork for an informal meeting, as part of Ireland's Presidency of the Council of the EU. Ireland's fishery and seafood sector employs 10,000 people directly, another 7,000 indirectly and is worth €1.25bn to the Irish economy every year. Earlier this month, a report to Marine Minister Timmy Dooley by consultant Kieran Mulvey, found the sector is facing an existential threat.

stories.title: Bank of Ireland's H1 pre-tax profits jump 33% to €960m
stories.summary: Bank of Ireland has reported a 33% jump in pre-tax profits for the six months to the end of June and said it was upgrading its guidance for the full year. Bank of Ireland said its half year pre-tax profits rose to €960m, and it also announced an interim dividend of 39 cent per share, an increase of 56%. Lending during the six month period rose by 4% to €84 billion. Bank of Ireland noted an "excellent" performance in its Irish lending which rose by €2.2 billion - up 7% - but it saw a fall of €0.5 billion in its UK lending where it said it prioritised value over volume.

stories.title: Missile that left crater in Poland probably Russian - PM
stories.summary: An object that came down in eastern Poland overnight appears to be a Russian missile, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk has said, after authorities found a crater and scattered debris in a field following reports of an explosion. It was the latest in a series of airspace incursions in countries on NATO's eastern flank, including Romania and the Baltic states, that have fuelled fears of the war in Ukraine spilling over the alliance's borders. Poland scrambled fighter jets to secure its airspace after Russian airstrikes killed at least eight people in neighbouring Ukraine, in attacks that extended as far as the western city of Lviv. "All the indications are that it was a Russian Kh-101 ballistic missile, but we want to be 100% certain about the type of missile and who launched it," Mr Tusk told an emergency meeting.

stories.title: Neligan voted best minor player of 2026 hurling season
stories.summary: Limerick's Xavier Neligan has been named the Electric Ireland Minor Star Hurling Player of the Year. Neligan is one of seven Treaty players in the team of the year. Limerick ended a 42-year wait to claim their first minor title since 1984, snatching victory from Munster rivals Tipperary with a 1-01 stoppage-time salvo to win on a 2-12 to 1-14 scoreline. Finalists Tipperary hold five selections, while semi-finalists Cork and Galway are also represented with one selection each and quarter-finalists Kilkenny also secure a spot.

stories.title: FA announce new 10-game ban for discrimination
stories.summary: Premier League players found guilty of discrimination face serving at least 10-game bans under enhanced Football Association rules. In past seasons, suspensions of between six and 12 games have been recommended for aggravated breaches – defined as any misconduct including an express or implied reference to ethnic origin, colour, race, nationality, religion, sex, gender, gender reassignment, sexual orientation or disability. The rules also apply to managers and other officials, and a statement read: "The FA is committed to delivering a game free from discrimination. "While significant progress has been made in recent years, discriminatory conduct continues to be a challenge across the game.

stories.title: What is the luteal phase, and why are women tracking it?
stories.summary: Women's reproductive health has undergone something of a PR transformation in recent years, with more discourse emerging around working with your hormones, tapping into the power of the period and what it all signifies about a woman's overall health. Google searches for the term 'luteal phase' have increased 300% in recent years, and a cursory glance at social media posts on the topic will see it blamed for everything from brain fog and sugar cravings to falling out of love with your partner. The luteal phase, Wallace says, is the second half of the menstrual cycle, spanning from ovulation (when an egg is released) to the next period.

stories.summary: The National Asset Management Agency (NAMA) will be dissolved at midnight tonight, 16 years after it was set up to take over the property loans of the Irish banks. The agency was established in December 2009 at the height of the financial collapse. It bought loans from the banks which had a face value of €72.3 billion. Controversially, it paid €31.8bn for the borrowings, a discount of 58% which left enormous holes in the balance sheets of the banks.

stories.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency has warned that thousands of people could be drinking water from private supplies that are not being monitored for contamination, posing an ongoing risk to public health. The agency is calling on the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage to change the law so that all private drinking water supplies must be registered with local authorities and routinely monitored. There are thousands of Small Private Water Supplies providing drinking water from wells and other private sources to schools, crèches, nursing homes, hotels, campsites, sports clubs and other commercial and public premises across Ireland. However, only about 1,600 are registered with local authorities - a requirement if the supplies are to be sampled and monitored to ensure the water is safe to drink.

stories.title: IAG second-quarter profit drops 16% on Iran war hit
stories.summary: British Airways owner IAG has reported a 16% drop in second-quarter profit, weighed down by soaring fuel costs and weak travel demand linked to the Middle East conflict, and said it now expects capacity to be flat this year. IAG, which also owns Iberia and Aer Lingus, said its fuel costs for the year would range between €8.3 billion and €8.6 billion, slightly lower than the roughly €9 billion forecast in May. The quarterly results reflect the pressure and uncertainty highlighted by fellow carriers Ryanair and EasyJet this month, as a prolonged and escalating war raises costs and weakens travel demand. All of IAG's airlines saw an adverse impact from higher fuel prices from March onwards, as fuel costs and emissions charges jumped nearly 23% in the second quarter to €2.22 billion, IAG said.

stories.title: Three firefighters dead and thousands evacuated in Greece
stories.summary: Thousands of people were evacuated last night as a fire that killed two firefighters threatened a tourist resort on the Greek island of Crete, while another firefighter died during efforts to put out a separate fire in mainland Greece. The fire south of the city of Rethymno, in the island's southwest, had forced officials to evacuate some 8,000 people overnight as it threatened the village resort of Agia Galini. Although the situation was improving today, Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis warned of "difficult days" ahead as the summer heat persists. Yiannis Tatarakis, mayor of the main outlying village of Agios Vassilios, said the Agia Galini resorts had reopened and visitors had been allowed to return.

stories.title: 100 Buildings: A Modernist surprise on the streets of Dungarvan
stories.summary: The Dungarvan Further Education and Training Centre is an unexpected Modern Movement gem in the suburbs of Dungarvan, County Waterford, on a corner site bounded by Wolfe Tone Road and O'Connell Street. If walking by, do look closer at the entrance for a sign of its past. In 1899, technical schools were set up in Ireland to provide more practical vocational training. The 1930 Vocational Education Act gave local councils the funds to develop technical education further with the building of bespoke vocational schools. Many charged nominal fees, which were small compared to the cost of going to secondary school. Free secondary school education was not available until 1967. In 1933, the Waterford County Surveyor, John Kingston Bowen (1888–1944), was tasked with designing a vocational school for Dungarvan. Scoil na gCeárd (translates to vocational school). The school building was officially opened on the 5th of April 1939, with Thomas Derrig (1897–1956), Minister for Education, in attendance. John was brother to Richard Bowen, County Surveyor for Kilkenny, who designed the Padmore and Barnes Boot Factory. The Waterford County VEC amalgamated with Wexford in 2011 and today the building is run by Dungarvan Further Education and Training Centre, which still provides training for adults across Waterford and Wexford. The school is a well-proportioned five-bay, two-storey, flat-roofed building in the International Style, with a single-bay, two-storey advanced entrance bay and a two-storey return. The entrance is sheltered by a concrete canopy, over which there is a rendered panel with raised lettering spelling out 'Scoil na gCeárd' in beautiful Gaelic letterform. The painted rendered walls give the building a clean appearance, and the low rendered boundary wall, piers, and pedestrian gate (blocked) still remain. All the windows were unfortunately replaced by uPVC casement windows in the early nineties. It is set back from the road, and its geometric form and massing are softened by mature trees.

stories.summary: Apple has forecast sales for the current quarter ending in September would grow more slowly than Wall Street targeted as the iPhone maker struggled to get the parts it needed to deliver products, and shares fell 5.5% in after-hours trade. Apple and the technology industry generally have been scrambling to meet demand for new products, especially those with high-end processors and memory, and executives described the weaker forecast in terms of supply, not demand. "We're seeing some very significant (supply) constraints currently with limited flexibility in the supply chain to remedy it," chief executive Tim Cook said during the call, adding that Apple was "evaluating all options" for alternative suppliers of memory chips. Chief Financial Officer Kevan Parekh told analysts on a call that Apple expects revenue growth of 9% to 11% in the quarter compared with a year earlier. That was less than the 12% rise predicted by Wall Street, according to LSEG data.

stories.title: Japan quake toll hits 28 as survivors struggle in heat
stories.summary: Japanese emergency workers were battling to rescue any remaining survivors from a devastated shopping centre, as the death toll from a major earthquake hit 28 and thousands sweltered in punishing heat. The government issued the new tally as officials said they have now extracted four bodies from the mass of rubble, steel and wires of the Aeon shopping centre, after a suspected gas blast following Tuesday's quake. At the shopping centre, "we have pulled out 10 people. Of them, four were confirmed dead. Another is without vital signs. Another five have suffered severe and minor injuries", an official from the disaster management office in the southwestern region said. Tuesday's 7.1-magnitude tremor caused widespread damage, flattening homes, damaging bridges, triggering fires and leaving tens of thousands of residents without power and water in temperatures forecast to hit 38C this weekend.

stories.title: Kenny and St Pat's need to take the next step
stories.summary: When Stephen Kenny walked into Richmond Park in May 2024, St Patrick's Athletic were not simply appointing another manager. They were making a statement about what they wanted to become. Kenny arrived with five League of Ireland titles on his CV, European group-stage experience and a reputation for building teams capable of dominating domestically rather than just competing. The first signs were initially rocky. I remember in one of his opening games against Dundalk his son, Eoin, came close to scoring and potentially getting the winner. Pat’s were eighth at the beginning of September 2024, yet they finished third after equalling a club record with nine consecutive league wins.
